name: אינטגרל מסוים בחלקים – x·cos(kx) עד כפולה של π (באנגלית)
questiontext:
Evaluate the following definite integral:

\( \displaystyle \int_{{CT:0}}^{{CT:1}} {{CT:2}}\,d{{CT:3}} = \) [[input:ans1]]
[[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: Find an antiderivative by integration by parts, then evaluate it at the limits.
Step 1 — Integration by parts
If

\[ \int f(x) dx = F(x) \]

then

\[ \int^a_b f(x) dx = F(a) - F(b). \]

So, we need to calculate

\[ \int {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}}. \]

Using integration by parts, that is if \(u\) and \(v\) are both functions of {{CT:4}} then

\[ \int u dv = uv - \int v du, \]

by defining \(u = {{CT:5}}\) and \(dv = {{CT:6}} d{{CT:3}}\) so that \(du = {{CT:7}} d{{CT:3}}\) and \(v = {{CT:8}}\). Then,

\[ \begin{aligned} \int {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} &= \int u dv \\ &= uv - \int v du \\ &= {{CT:5}}\left[{{CT:8}}\right] - \int \left[{{CT:8}}\right]\cdot \left({{CT:7}}\right) d{{CT:3}} \\ &= {{CT:9}} - \int {{CT:10}} d{{CT:3}} \\ &= {{CT:11}} \end{aligned} \]

Step 2 — Evaluating at the limits
So, let \(F({{CT:3}}) = {{CT:12}}\) Then,

\[ \begin{aligned} \int^{{CT:1}}_{{CT:0}} {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} &= F({{CT:1}}) - F({{CT:0}}) \\ &= {{CT:13}} - {{CT:14}} \\ &= {{CT:15}} \end{aligned} \]

on_true.feedback: Remember, this is a definite integration problem so your answer should be a number.
